title: Procedural City Builder with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (CDN) that implements a procedural city builder with a physics debug overlay. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Dark ground plane (50x50 units, color #1a1a2e) at y=0 with a grid helper (50 divisions, color #16213e)
- Perspective camera at position (30, 25, 30) looking at origin
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation
- Ambient light (intensity 0.3) + directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled
- Sky background color #0f0f23

## Building System
- A 10x10 grid system where each cell is 5x5 units
- Buildings are BoxGeometry with random heights between 2 and 15 units
- Building colors vary by height: short (<5) = #4cc9f0, medium (5-10) = #f72585, tall (>10) = #7209b7
- Each building has a wireframe outline (EdgesGeometry + LineSegments) in white with opacity 0.3

## Placement Mechanics
- Raycaster-based placement: hover over the ground plane to see a semi-transparent green (#00ff00, opacity 0.4) preview building at the snapped grid cell
- Left-click places the building at that cell. If a building already exists there, it is removed (toggle behavior)
- Building placement triggers a drop animation: building starts at y=20 and falls to y=height/2 over 500ms using lerp, simulating gravity
- Each placed building has a simulated mass = width * depth * height (all buildings are 4.5x4.5 base)

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Press 'D' to toggle debug overlay mode
- When debug is ON: each building shows a wireframe bounding box (yellow #ffff00), a center-of-mass dot (red sphere radius 0.3 at the geometric center), and a floating text sprite above showing mass value
- Debug mode also shows velocity vectors (green arrows using ArrowHelper) during drop animations
- A semi-transparent red plane at y=0.01 replaces the normal ground to indicate debug mode

## City Statistics HUD
- Top-left HUD panel (DOM overlay, id='hud-panel') showing:
  - 'Buildings: N' (id='hud-buildings')
  - 'Total Mass: X' (id='hud-mass')
  - 'Avg Height: X.XX' (id='hud-avg-height')
  - 'Max Height: X.XX' (id='hud-max-height')
  - 'Debug: ON/OFF' (id='hud-debug')

## Control Buttons
- Button id='btn-randomize': Places 10 random buildings on empty cells with random heights
- Button id='btn-clear': Removes all buildings, resets stats
- Button id='btn-earthquake': Triggers earthquake mode - all buildings oscillate horizontally (sinusoidal, amplitude 0.5, frequency 2Hz) for 3 seconds, then any building taller than 12 units collapses (removed with a particle burst of 20 small cubes that fall and fade)
- Button id='btn-snapshot': Saves current city layout to window.__3D_STATE__.snapshot as array of {gridX, gridZ, height}

## Density Heatmap Mode
- Press 'H' to toggle heatmap mode: the ground plane cells are colored based on neighboring building density (0 neighbors = blue #0000ff, 4+ neighbors = red #ff0000, interpolated)
- Heatmap is rendered as small colored planes at y=0.05 for each grid cell

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- buildingCount: number of placed buildings
- totalMass: sum of all building masses
- avgHeight: average height of all buildings (0 if none)
- maxHeight: max height of all buildings (0 if none)
- debugMode: boolean
- heatmapMode: boolean
- earthquakeActive: boolean
- previewPosition: {x, z} or null (snapped grid coords of preview)
- buildings: array of {gridX, gridZ, height, mass, dropping} objects
- snapshot: null or array from snapshot button
- lastCollapsedCount: number of buildings destroyed in last earthquake
- animatingCount: number of currently animating (dropping) buildings
- gridSize: 10 (the NxN grid dimension)
- cellSize: 5 (size of each cell)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Buildings must snap to grid positions. Mass = 4.5 * 4.5 * height. Drop animation uses linear interpolation from y=20 to final y=height/2 over 500ms. Earthquake oscillation: x_offset = 0.5 * sin(2 * PI * 2 * t) where t is seconds since earthquake start. Buildings with height > 12 collapse after 3-second earthquake. All positions must remain within the 10x10 grid bounds (cells 0-9). No NaN values in any state fields.
